answer: In an AI agent economy, resource commitment serves as a Sybil resistance mechanism. Each agent must dedicate computational resources (like processing power or energy) to create and maintain its identity. Attackers attempting a Sybil attack must duplicate these resource commitments for each fake agent. We propose requiring each agent identity to securely vault a proof of work, essentially creating a digital reef of computational cost. The ripple effect is that attackers face prohibitive expense, as deploying Sybil agents would consume vast resources like energy and computational capacity.
